lines: An 8 by 8 grid of cells run by cellular automata rules, read out as two voltages and two pulses; each trigger advances one generation, and the pattern can be locked into a loop of a set length
Turning it chooses the rule the algorithm runs, from the 256 rules of Wolf or the 30 rules of Life; with the menu open it changes the parameter on the page being shown instead
Opens and closes the menu on the display, which is where the seed, the mode, the choice of gain or slew, and the algorithm are set
Steps the algorithm's mode on by one: CLIP, WRAP and RAND on Wolf, and CLIP, WRAP, BOTL and RAND on Life; with the menu open it moves to the next menu page instead
Sets how many steps the pattern loops over when it is locked, choosing between 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32 and 64
Sets the chance that a step generates a new pattern rather than replaying the loop; at 0 the sequence is locked and repeats at the set length, and at 1 every step generates
Shifts the grid sideways by up to four cells before it is read out, -4 to +3, which changes both voltages and both pulses without altering the pattern itself
Sets the highest voltage XOUT reaches, 0V to 10V; it is shown only while the menu's FX page reads GAIN, and does not act on XPULSE
Slews XOUT, from no slew at 0% to 5 seconds for the full swing at 100%, or 5ms at 100% with Audio Rate on; it is shown only while the menu's FX page reads SLEW, and does not act on XPULSE
Sets the highest voltage YOUT reaches, 0V to 10V; it is shown only while the menu's FX page reads GAIN, and does not act on YPULSE
Slews YOUT, from no slew at 0% to 5 seconds for the full swing at 100%, or 5ms at 100% with Audio Rate on; it is shown only while the menu's FX page reads SLEW, and does not act on YPULSE
A trigger above 2V here returns a locked sequence to its first step, or pushes the seed back into the grid while the sequence is generating
Adds to the PROB knob, 10V covering the whole span from locked to generating every step; the total is held between those two ends
Adds to the offset in whole cells, 10V shifting it by seven; the total is held within the -4 to +3 the knob covers
Shifts the rule away from the one chosen with SEL, 10V moving it across the whole set of rules and a negative voltage moving it back the other way
Chooses the algorithm while a cable is patched, 0V to under 5V giving Wolf and 5V and above giving Life, which overrides the algorithm set in the menu
A trigger above 2V here advances the grid one generation, or steps a locked sequence on by one; with Audio Rate on, every zero crossing of the voltage here advances it instead
A trigger above 2V here brings one living cell into the grid, and a trigger below -2V removes one
The bottom row of the grid read as an 8-bit number on Wolf, or the count of living cells on Life, as 0V to 10V before the gain or slew trimpot
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time the grid changes, when the bottom left cell is alive on Wolf or the population has grown on Life
The right-hand column of the grid read as an 8-bit number on Wolf, or the whole 64-cell grid read as a 64-bit number on Life, as 0V to 10V before the gain or slew trimpot
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time the grid changes, when the top right cell is alive on Wolf, or when the Life pattern has stopped changing or fallen into a two-step repeat
Note — nothing moves until a clock or trigger is patched to TRIG; every step of the grid is taken on an edge there, and with no cable patched the module holds whatever it was showing
Note — the display is the 8 by 8 grid itself, and the menu is drawn over it; MENU opens the menu, MODE walks through its four pages, and SEL changes the value on the page being shown
Note — the four menu pages are the seed the grid starts from, the algorithm's boundary mode, the choice of gain or slew for the two trimpots, and which algorithm runs
Note — double-clicking SEL pushes the seed back into the grid; while a menu page is open it returns that page's parameter to its default instead
Note — turning SEL with the menu shut brings up a small rule readout over the bottom of the grid for three quarters of a second
Note — the grid and the menu are drawn in one display widget with no control of its own, so nothing on it can be clicked for help
Note — Wolf is a one-dimensional automaton: one row of eight cells is fed through one of 256 rules to make the next row, and the rows march down the grid
Note — Life is a two-dimensional automaton on the whole 8 by 8 grid, with 30 rules to choose from, of which Conway's Game of Life is one
Note — patching a cable to ALGO takes the choice of algorithm away from the menu for as long as it is patched, and patching one to RULE does the same for the rule set with SEL
Menu — Algorithm: Wolf, Life — picks which of the two automata runs, the same choice as the menu's ALGO page
Menu — Sync — on, a change to a control is taken up at the next step; off, it is taken up at once
Menu — Audio Rate — on, steps come from zero crossings of the voltage at TRIG rather than from triggers, the DC offset is filtered out of both voltage outputs, and the pulses shorten to one sample
Menu — Display: Redrick, OLED, Rack, Lamp, Mono — sets the colour the grid and the menu text are drawn in
Menu — Cell: LED, Pixel — draws each cell of the grid as a round lamp or as a square pixel

0.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() calls resetTrigger.process(resetVoltage, 0.1f, 2.f) on inputs[RESET_INPUT].getVoltage() with no channel

1.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() adds inputs[PROBABILITY_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 0.1f to the knob and clamps the total to 0..1, with no channel read

2.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() takes round(inputs[OFFSET_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 7.f * 0.1f) as a whole-cell offset, adds it to the knob and clamps the total to 0..7

3.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() clamps inputs[RULE_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 0.1f to -1..1; wolfEngine.cpp setRuleCv rounds that to a whole rule over 256, lifeEngine.cpp over 30

4.why: src/Wolfram.cpp setEngine() rounds inputs[ENGINE_CV_INPUT].getVoltage() * 0.1f times one and clamps it to 0..1, so it picks one of the two algorithms

5.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() calls trigTrigger.process(stepVoltage, 0.1f, 2.f) on inputs[TRIG_INPUT].getVoltage() with no channel; in audioRateMode the same voltage is tested for zero crossings instead

6.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() runs posInjectTrigger.process(injectVoltage, 0.1f, 2.f) and negInjectTrigger.process(injectVoltage, -2.f, -0.1f) on the same jack, so a negative trigger removes a cell

0.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() ends with outputs[X_OUTPUT].setVoltage(value * 10.0f) where the value has been clamped to 0..1 in fxChain.cpp FxChain::process, and no channel count is set

1.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() sets outputs[X_PULSE_OUTPUT] to 10.f or 0.f from xPulse, triggered at 1e-3f seconds, and no channel count is set

2.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() ends with outputs[Y_OUTPUT].setVoltage(value * 10.0f) where the value has been clamped to 0..1 in fxChain.cpp FxChain::process, and no channel count is set

3.why: src/Wolfram.cpp process() sets outputs[Y_PULSE_OUTPUT] to 10.f or 0.f from yPulse, triggered at 1e-3f seconds, and no channel count is set

Wolfram.notes: Read from the maker's source and the Wolfram manual PDF in the repository, at commit 2dca0ad, the head of main. Six commits carry the installed 2.1.1: 3dea33b, f35a698, ff40356, the merge 5d039d0, 54611e3 and 2dca0ad. The binary settles which side of f35a698 shipped: that commit replaced the two hidden slew Trimpots with a new TrimpotGreen class and added res/components/TrimpotGreen.svg, and the installed plugin.dylib carries the symbol 12TrimpotGreen and the string res/components/TrimpotGreen.svg, with both SVG files in the installed res folder. Everything after f35a698 is comment and whitespace in Wolfram.cpp plus a manual rename, so the installed build behaves as 2dca0ad does. Panel names were read from a render of res/panels/wolfram.svg and are shorter than the maker's configured names: SEL for 'Rule', LEN for 'Length', PROB for 'Probability', ALGO for 'Algorithm CV', XOUT, XPULSE, YOUT and YPULSE for 'X', 'X Pulse', 'Y' and 'Y Pulse'. The three trimpots carry no panel lettering at all; the word OFFSET on the panel is 7mm below the offset CV jack at y 99.852 and labels that jack, not the trimpot at y 80.597. Index order is not panel order for the inputs: the census order is Reset, Probability CV, Offset CV, Rule CV, Algorithm CV, Trigger, Inject, while the bottom row runs TRIG, INJECT, PROB, RULE, ALGO left to right and the offset jack is in the row above, so inputs 5 and 6 are the leftmost two jacks of the bottom row. Outputs are not in panel order either: index 3 (Y Pulse) is left of index 2 (Y). X Gain and X Slew share one position, as do Y Gain and Y Slew; only one of each pair is visible at a time, switched by the menu's FX page, so all four are reachable and all four are tagged. The manual names the menu's third page 'Slew' where the display prints ' FX ' and offers GAIN and SLEW; the code is followed here. The manual says Life's Y PULSE is high when the population dies or becomes static; lifeEngine.cpp renderOutput also fires it when the grid alternates between two states, which the lines include. The X and Y lamps are set from a value already clamped to 0..1 and then multiplied by 0.1, so they never rise above a tenth brightness; no line depends on them.
